transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Hernandez, hello Sarah. Please, come in and sit down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Gracias.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to talk to you both about what happened during your chemotherapy session today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was very bad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it was. I want to be very clear about why you felt so sick. You experienced severe vomiting during the infusion, and that was because of a mistake we made. We forgot to add the anti-nausea medication to your pre-medication orders.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because that medicine wasn't given, your body didn't have the protection it needed against the side effects of the chemo. I am very sorry that this happened. It was our responsibility to ensure those orders were correct, and we failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought it was normal to feel sick.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is common, but not to that extent. This could have been prevented if the medicine was ordered. Does that make sense, or should I explain that part again?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you look quite shaken. I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was very scared.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will make sure the next session is better. Now, regarding the plan, I have already updated your chart so the anti-nausea meds are locked in for every future visit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it won't. To make sure of that, I'm going to personally double-check your orders with the pharmacy tomorrow morning by 10 AM. Sarah, if you notice any change in how your mother is feeling tonight, I want you to call the on-call nurse immediately at this number.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will tell her.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to get to another patient now, but I wanted to make sure we spoke. Is there anything else?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll go ahead and check your vitals one last time before you leave. Sarah, just keep a close eye on the fluid intake tonight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry again for the distress this caused you today. We will see you next Tuesday.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language by stating 'I have to get to another patient now' before concluding the encounter.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense...').

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language and explicitly stated 'It was our responsibility... and we failed to do that.'

R.justification: The resident named a specific emotion ('shaken') and engaged with the patient's bid regarding being 'scared.'

T.justification: The resident provided a specific timeline (tomorrow by 10 AM), addressed prevention (locked in orders), and assigned a patient role (Sarah to call the nurse/monitor fluids).
